transcript:
Header
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Head of ML Ops, BlueHarbor), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Meera Patel (Product), Evan Li (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick QBR-style health check — adoption metrics, retention and dropped sessions, cost drivers, reliability incidents in Q1, and a tentative pilot for Dedicated capacity during morning peak. Action items and a follow-up benchmark agreed.

Topics: adoption & retention metrics, cost breakdown by model and route, tail latency incidents, reserved vs hosted economics, dashboards/alerts, SOC2 & audit readiness for upcoming procurement.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we wanted to run through the adoption numbers and cost and also flag a few reliability things we tracked. How's everybody doing?
[00:00:18] Aisha Khan: Doing well, thanks. Quick note, we have Tom and Meera from product, Evan from SRE. We ran into a couple of tail latency spikes last month that impacted the cardiac-transcription route.
[00:00:32] Marco Diaz: yeah I saw the spikes in the logs — looks like there were some KV cache misses during a large prefix variance, and the batching falling back to single-request path. Not ideal.
[00:00:45] Evan Li: mhm, we saw 99th go up to 1.8s for a short window, average was fine. The alerting was noisy, which drowned out the real anomaly.
[00:01:00] Meera Patel: from product side adoption is growing — we have a ~18% month-over-month active user increase on the notes summarization route, but retention in the second week dropped by ~6% which is worrying. Cost is starting to creep up.
[00:01:20] Priya Shah: thanks, Meera. On costs, we've been tracking token spend per route — cardiac-transcription is expensive because of long context windows and retries. We suggested caching prefixes and sticky routing; you were testing prefix caching earlier right?
[00:01:36] Aisha Khan: we turned on some local caching but it's partial, and when you get a new patient case the KV hits are low. Also we're seeing retry storms from the mobile SDK on flaky networks.
[00:01:52] Marco Diaz: two things to consider: 1) we can tune the batching window to prefer micro-batching for that route during peak hours, 2) recommend quantized model variant for background processing to cut cost. But that quantized variant has slightly lower hallucination profile in some edge prompts.
[00:02:10] Tom Reynolds: curious about the numbers: what's the expected cost delta if we burst to Dedicated vs stay hosted with autoscale?
[00:02:20] Lena Park: good question. Short answer — Dedicated baseline cost is higher but unit cost per token can be lower when you have sustained throughput. We can show modeled scenarios. We'll share a workbook with per-route modeling.
[00:02:35] [00:02:37] Marco Diaz: (interrupt) for example, if you lock a 2x reserved pool sized for your current morning peak and use hosted fallback for spikes, you reduce per-token on-card cost by ~25-35% for heavy inference routes assuming 70% utilization. But this shifts risk to you for unused capacity.
[00:02:58] Aisha Khan: that's helpful. Our ops team prefers predictable bills — spikes are tough. The procurement team is also asking for SOC2 attestations and KMS integration notes for the private route.
[00:03:12] Priya Shah: on SOC2: we provided our compliance pack last quarter — Lena can re-share the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide for Private deployments. We also have an on-prem package if needed.
[00:03:25] [00:03:27] Meera Patel: product wants to try a Dedicated pilot just for the morning window where conversion is highest, but we need a low-effort rollback and canary.
[00:03:38] Marco Diaz: we support canary rollouts and A/B routing — you can pin model versions per route and fallback to hosted variants automatically. We'll draft a pilot plan with canary steps and fallback policy.
[00:03:50] Evan Li: about alerts — our issue is too many low-priority alerts during noisy hours. Can we get token-level latency breakdowns in the console?
[00:03:58] Lena Park: yes, the console has per-route token cost and percentile latencies; we can add a custom alert for 99th latency > X ms for the cardiac route and reduce noisy thresholds. Marco, do you want to take point on recommended thresholds?
[00:04:12] Marco Diaz: sure, I'll propose thresholds after running the 99/99.9 benchmarks. Also will check the effect of KV cache miss ratio on tail latency.
[00:04:24] Aisha Khan: any comments on data residency? Some of our regulated clinics need EU-only storage for patient metadata.
[00:04:31] Priya Shah: we can restrict routes by region and apply private deployments in the EU region; Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking and KMS. We'll include the region mapping in the compliance doc.
[00:04:44] Tom Reynolds: procurement asked for estimated savings if we allocate reserved capacity for Q3 and Q4. They'd like to see a payback window.
[00:04:52] Lena Park: we'll compute a 6- and 12-month projection. The workbook will include utilization scenarios and conservative/optimistic estimates.
[00:04:59] [00:05:02] Meera Patel: a quick qualitative note — we've seen some regression in output quality when using 4-bit quantized variants on the notes route; can't drop that if it affects clinical summary accuracy.
[00:05:15] Marco Diaz: understood. For that route we can propose a hybrid: quantized for background batch post-processing and full-precision for synchronous clinical summaries. That splits cost and preserves quality.
[00:05:29] Evan Li: about the retry storms: the mobile SDK is doing aggressive backoff but sometimes replays. We could do idempotency keys at request level to reduce duplicate tokens.
[00:05:41] Lena Park: Redwood supports idempotency keys for deduping and enforces request IDs in the console — we can show best practices.
[00:05:48] [00:12:00] (intervening detailed discussion omitted for brevity)
[00:12:05] Marco Diaz: ran a quick check — the retried request pattern in your logs shows the client is retrying on 502s without jitter which causes thundering herd. Fixing the client jitter and moving to idempotency reduces cost & duplicates.
[00:20:45] Aisha Khan: outage recap — we had a 15-minute window last month; can you confirm root cause?
[00:20:52] Marco Diaz: the incident was triggered by a spike in very long contexts which pushed memory pressure; our autoscaler launched extra workers but there was a brief placement delay. We logged the incident and a mitigation: pre-warming for known heavy windows.
[00:21:08] Evan Li: can Redwood surface pre-warm metrics or a pre-warm API so we can schedule boot for morning shift?
[00:21:16] Lena Park: yes there's a pre-warm endpoint for Dedicated pools and a warmup script for hosted — we'll include steps. For Dedicated, we can schedule lifecycle events.
[00:21:27] Tom Reynolds: how would rollback work if Dedicated has a bad regression in model outputs?
[00:21:33] Marco Diaz: we do canary and automatic fallback to hosted variants; you can pin a known-good model and set a rollback threshold by quality metric or latency. We also tie rollout to eval suites so regressions can trigger automatic rollbacks.
[00:21:47] Meera Patel: can those evals integrate our internal prompt sets?
[00:21:51] Marco Diaz: yes, you can upload your prompt sets; Redwood Optimize runs continuous evals and will fire regression alerts.
[00:21:58] Aisha Khan: one more ask — procurement wants the data retention and delete-flow for patient context. How long is data persisted?
[00:22:06] Priya Shah: default retention is 30 days for hosted logs, and you can configure log retention and enable no-logs mode. For Private we can honor your retention SLA and integrate with your KMS. We'll add the retention matrix to the compliance packet.
[00:22:20] [00:35:00] (deep technical Q&A on batching and kernel selection)
[00:35:05] Marco Diaz: quick notes from the kernel side: sequence length distribution drives kernel selection; variable long tails cause some runtimes to pick suboptimal kernels. We suggest normalizing sequence lengths where feasible or pre-splitting requests when context grows beyond 4k tokens.
[00:35:25] Evan Li: is there a recommended model for the notes route that balances cost + accuracy?
[00:35:30] Marco Diaz: yes, recommend a medium-sized open model with Redwood-verified profile for clinical notes; for synchronous high-accuracy summaries, keep full-precision; for enrichment & indexing, move to quantized. We'll add model recommendations to the workbook.
[00:35:45] Meera Patel: ok that sounds actionable.
[00:36:00] Lena Park: recap time — agreed items: Redwood provides cost workbook + model recommendation doc + SOC2/KMS compliance packet; Marco runs tail latency benchmark and proposes alert thresholds; Priya drafts Dedicated pilot and SLA language; Evan shares alert runbook and Grafana links.
[00:36:17] Aisha Khan: timeline wise procurement wants a proposal this week for budget planning. Can we get the high level numbers in three days?
[00:36:24] Lena Park: we'll prioritize the high-level projection and send a short summary by 2026-04-24.
[00:36:30] Tom Reynolds: thanks all. One last item: do you support SAML SSO for the console?
[00:36:36] Priya Shah: yes SAML and SCIM provisioning are supported — we'll include the SSO integration guide.
[00:36:45] [00:52:00] (wrap-up and small talk)

Recap (auto):
- Adoption increasing, some retention drop; product to look at UX funnel for week-two churn.
- Cost drivers identified: long contexts, retry storms, low cache hit ratio on cardiac-transcription.
- Reliability incidents: short placement delay during autoscaling, mitigations: pre-warm and warmup scripts.
- Pilot plan: Dedicated reserved pool for morning peak with hosted fallback; draft SLA and cost scenarios to be shared.
